macro_summary: The S&P 500 is near all-time highs (~7,786–7,800) but the macro backdrop is tense: July CPI printed 3.4% YoY / core 2.5%, in-line with estimates, cementing a Fed hold at September's meeting but keeping a hike later in 2026 firmly on the table. The July FOMC vote was a divided 9-3, with three dissenters arguing for an immediate hike, and long yields have repriced sharply — the 10-year topped 4.7% and the 30-year hit 5.25%. The next major macro inflection point is Jackson Hole (Aug 27–29), where Chair Warsh delivers his first keynote as Fed chair on Aug 28 — one day after NVDA's earnings — compressing two major market-moving events into a 48-hour window. News flow this week is front-loaded with three high-conviction setups, all grounded in confirmed near-term catalysts.

ideas.name: NVIDIA Corporation
ideas.thesis: NVDA reports Q2 FY2027 earnings on Aug 26 AMC with consensus expecting $93.6B in revenue — a figure that would confirm the hyperscaler AI capex wave is translating directly into Nvidia's top line. The Vera Rubin platform transition and ~80% AI accelerator market share give the company pricing power that is not yet fully reflected at the current price vs analyst targets. The Jackson Hole keynote lands Aug 28, just 36 hours after earnings, meaning a strong print + a dovish-leaning Warsh could be a powerful sequential catalyst; conversely, a hawkish signal is the primary risk.
ideas.catalyst: Q2 FY2027 earnings report August 26, 2026 after market close — EPS consensus $2.13, revenue consensus $93.6B
ideas.edge: 36 analysts carry a Strong Buy consensus; MarketBeat mean target $305.94 and Yahoo Finance mean ~$309 vs $225.16 Polygon prev close — implied upside of ~36–37%. EPS estimates revised up 7.8% over the past 90 days. Options are liquid and well-suited for a defined-risk pre-earnings play (e.g., a bull call spread expiring after Aug 26 to cap premium at risk).
ideas.bull_case: Big Tech CapEx guided at ~$725B in 2026 (+77% YoY) and NVDA is positioned to capture 35–40% of that spend; a beat-and-raise on Aug 26 — combined with a non-hawkish Warsh at Jackson Hole — could drive a rapid re-rate toward the $300 analyst targets Bernstein and Wells Fargo have already published.
ideas.bear_case: The stock has already run ~17–20% YTD; any sign of demand moderation, Vera Rubin supply delays, or a hawkish Warsh speech the following morning could trigger a sharp post-earnings reversal. Three Fed dissenters and sticky mid-3% inflation are a real rate-hike tail risk into Q4.

ideas.name: Reddit, Inc.
ideas.thesis: Reddit formally joins the S&P 500 before Monday's open on Aug 18, forcing index funds and passive ETFs tracking the benchmark to accumulate shares — a structural, non-discretionary demand event. The stock surged ~12–14% on Friday to ~$178 on the announcement, but the forced-buying flow from index rebalancers typically continues through and just past the effective inclusion date, not just on the announcement day. Q2 beat on revenue and Q3 guidance came in above consensus, giving the fundamental story credibility alongside the technical tailwind.
ideas.catalyst: S&P 500 index inclusion effective before market open Monday August 18, 2026 — triggers mandatory passive-fund buying from all S&P 500 trackers
ideas.edge: 12 analysts carry a median price target of $227.50 vs current price ~$178 (per Investing.com Aug 15 data), implying ~28% upside to median. DA Davidson holds $200 target with Buy; Wedbush maintains Best Ideas List inclusion. Options are available for defined-risk expression — a short-dated call spread (e.g., Aug 22 expiry) or a risk-reversal captures the inclusion pop without full downside exposure to post-inclusion selling.
ideas.bull_case: S&P inclusion forces a sustained multi-day rebalancing bid from the largest passive funds; if the Google AI traffic overhang stabilizes and ad revenue execution continues (Q2 and Q3 guidance both beat), RDDT re-rates toward the $215–$228 analyst median, representing a swing-trade return of 20%+ from current levels.
ideas.bear_case: The 11–14% Friday pop has already front-run a significant portion of the inclusion demand; post-inclusion 'sell the news' selling by momentum traders is well-documented historically. Google AI search changes remain a structural overhang on traffic and data-licensing revenue, and a major hedge fund (Marshall Wace) cut its position by 41.6% in Q2 2026.
ideas.conviction_note: Downgraded from high to medium: the catalyst (S&P 500 index inclusion) is a structural flow event, not a specific dated fundamental catalyst such as an earnings release or Fed decision. No specific earnings date or policy decision with a definitive outcome anchors the conviction.

ideas.name: Analog Devices, Inc.
ideas.thesis: ADI reports Q3 FY2026 earnings before the open on Aug 19, with consensus calling for EPS of $3.33 — a +62% year-over-year increase — and revenue of $3.93B vs $2.88B a year ago. The Q2 beat (revenue +37% YoY, exceeding consensus) and a Zacks Strong Buy rank heading into the print suggest estimate momentum is real. ADI fits this portfolio's semiconductor focus and benefits from AI infrastructure buildout, industrial recovery, and the Empower Semiconductor acquisition for AI power delivery.
ideas.catalyst: Q3 FY2026 earnings August 19, 2026 before market open — EPS consensus $3.33 (+62% YoY), revenue consensus $3.93B
ideas.edge: Consensus analyst target $441–$457 (StockAnalysis 33-analyst mean: $457.73) vs ~$384 recent price — ~15–19% implied upside to the mean. The stock's 56x trailing P/E and 41.8% YTD run leave it exposed to a sell-the-news reaction even on an in-line print; a hawkish macro read from the Aug 19 FOMC minutes release (same day) could compound downside.
